Not long ago, the writer and nature lover Armand left Bloomville and ventured deep into the Beardow Woods.
There, he discovered the gentle yet powerful Princess Melloblum, and her six Budsquires.
Imagine his surprise at this discovery, because this area of the forest was known to be home to the ill-tempered Cubbo Family, who did not get along well with others, and tended to force their neighbors off their land.
Upon further observation, Armand noticed a flower seedling growing on the land where Princess Melloblum and her Budsquires lived.
It emitted a faint fragrance, reminiscent of snow, with a lingering scent of joy.
Armand noted that the Cubbo Family seemed reluctant to approach the seedling.
"Lucky," Armand thought, "that nature favors the beautiful."
...
Later, Armand realized that he, too, was blessed by fortune.
Because Budsquires happened to be the only family he could twine with.
After twining with them, he became the seventh Budsquire, devoted to Princess Melloblum.
...
From that day on, the tale of "Princess Melloblum and the Seven Budsquires" began to spread through Beardow Woods.
And Armand enjoyed an idyllic time living in the forest.
